decision_shape.answer: The signal — but taken by POLL, not by push. Not the TTL, and not NAT.Reset() driven from the watcher. One mechanism ships; no TTL floor was added.
decision_shape.mechanism: bypass.NAT records the interface name Control bound each socket to (socket.iface) and, on every Send, compares it with what Config.Interface returns now (outbound.Selector.Interface in production). Mismatch closes every socket whose binding differs; the next Send re-dials with the current binding. internal/bypass/bypass.go: Config.Interface, socket.iface, currentInterface(), rebindLocked().
arguments_strongest_first: It is the same signal, not a timer. Selector.Interface() is not an independent poll of the OS — it is the published output of the very rtnetlink watcher a push would have come from: watch() receives RouteUpdate/LinkUpdate, calls refresh(), set() stores the name under s.mu. Reading that field reads the result of the event.

Poll beats push on precision: Reset() fires on ANY watcher event (and an active network produces many that are not interface changes), closing every socket each time. Comparing names fires exactly when the interface is genuinely different.

The TTL treats the symptom (a wedged socket), not the cause, and pays blind: too short tears down healthy exchanges, too long leaves the leak window open, and no value is derivable from anything. It is not needed as a floor either — the signal cannot 'fail to arrive', because nothing waits for it: it is read on every Send, i.e. exactly when a stale binding could first do harm.
It cost one optional field in bypass.Config and one passthrough in agent/wire.go. internal/outbound is unchanged.

decision_scope_argument_did_not_hold.claim_that_was_deferred_on: 'Doing it properly means touching the rtnetlink watcher outbound.Selector, which widens the pass beyond BypassSink.'
decision_scope_argument_did_not_hold.verdict: False in its premise, checked rather than taken on trust. Everything a push would have delivered is already published: Selector.Interface() is exported, kept under RWMutex, updated by the watcher, and ALREADY handed to the agent as Config.Physical (cmd/hop/main.go passes physical.Interface). The correct shape is cheaper than the shape whose expense justified the deferral.

decision_own_flag.answer: Own flag, bypass_rebind. bypass_sink — the plausible reuse candidate named by the previous HANDOFF — was NOT reused.
arguments: Mechanical, not aesthetic: bypass_sink=off makes Send return ErrDisabled on its first line, before any socket exists. The guard would go red under it for the wrong cause — 'nothing left the machine at all', not 'the socket did not change' — and would not distinguish a broken rebind from a switched-off path.
negcheck loses resolution on reuse: 'red without bypass_sink' would stop naming one cause.
Same argument the previous pass used to keep bypass_tcp_reject out of reject_mode. The line the codebase draws: one flag, one claim.
decision_own_flag.registered: internal/policy/policies.go, next to BypassSink and BypassTCPReject. Two guards, both written and SEEN RED before the implementation, in a separate commit (0dbf087) — the order the last three passes followed. Red on the assertion, not on compilation: the Config.Interface field and the agent passthrough went into that same commit precisely so the claim failed rather than the build.

changed_files.what: New InterfaceFunc type and optional Config.Interface. socket gains iface (written once at creation — the binding is immutable, §6.8). currentInterface() reads the callback BEFORE taking n.mu (foreign callback, own lock) and reports 'unknown' for nil callback, error, or empty name. rebindLocked(iface) runs in socketFor under policy.BypassRebind and closes every socket whose non-empty iface differs, counting n.rebound. Stats gains Rebound.

Up() passes Interface: bypass.InterfaceFunc(a.cfg.Physical) into bypass.New — a passthrough of a value the agent already held, not a new event source. A nil Config.Physical converts to a nil InterfaceFunc and the NAT behaves exactly as before.
New policy BypassRebind (bypass_rebind), registered in All(). Doc carries the short form of why it is not bypass_sink.

new_tests.note: TestBypassInterfaceChangeRebindsSocket is a registered guard. The seen-is-refreshed-on-Send trap is closed twice over: the fake clock NEVER advances (sweepLocked cannot run at all while now.Sub(swept) < idle/2, so the idle sweep has nobody to collect — and the test asserts clk.Now() unchanged at the end), and the client keeps sending across the change, asserting the port does NOT move while the interface is stable and DOES move once it changes. Observable is the source port the listener sees, via listener.SetReadDeadline — fakenet.Bypass.WaitPackets is used nowhere, it waits forever. TestBypassIdleSweepNeverCollectsSocketUnderTraffic is documentation, not a guard: green under either state of the flag, it shows the sweep running on every Send for 7.5×Idle and never collecting the socket.

W47, the second registered guard: the Config.Physical → bypass.Config.Interface seam. Needed because Config.Interface is optional — a forgotten passthrough would leave the mechanism dead in production with the unit test green. Drives a real agent on a fake device with a listener on loopback and flips the interface name under live traffic.

stayed_green: the whole internal/bypass suite — the existing tests pass no Config.Interface, so socket.iface is empty and never counts as stale: exactly the pre-policy behavior
TestBypassSendErrorCountsAsBlocked (internal/netstack) — untouched, the UDP refusal path did not move
deviations: The signal is polled, not pushed — a departure from the shape the previous HANDOFF named first (NAT.Reset() from the watcher). Rejected in favour of something cheaper and more precise; argument in implementation-notes.md. Conservative in CLAUDE.md's sense: no new event source, no new goroutine, no change to the platform package.

The comparison runs on Send, so other clients' stale sockets are closed at the first Send by any client. While the NAT is entirely silent, stale sockets live on — harmless outbound (nothing goes out through them), with one residue: a receive goroutine could still accept a reply on the old interface in that window. That is exactly why the first Send closes ALL sockets with a foreign binding, not only the one it came for.

Stats grew a third field (Rebound) in a struct nothing in production reads yet (Stack.Stats does not fold it in — that is the next queue item). Added because the guard asserts the mechanism fired directly, not only via the port change.
spec_edits: SPEC.md §6.8: new paragraph 'Следствие первое распространяется и на долгоживущие сокеты bypass' — the NAT remembers its binding, compares it on every send, closes what diverged; the idle sweep cannot play this role because service discovery retries continuously; a missing default route is not an interface change.
No §8.3 row: the claim is unit-level, exactly like both bypass_sink guards. No numbered T test was added.
not_done_on_purpose: No L3 stand with a second veth (the shape HANDOFF suggested). It would exercise the kernel's SO_BINDTODEVICE rather than the decision to re-open the socket, and the kernel side of that path is already covered by T31.
No TTL. See decision_shape — shipping both without naming the load-bearing one is what the task forbade, and the TTL is not needed as a floor.

next_task.name: Surface bypass.NAT.Stats() through netstack.Stack.Stats()
next_task.why_first: It is the last piece of the bypass path that is invisible rather than absent, and this pass just made it worse in one specific way: bypass.Stats now carries three counters (Sockets, Orphaned, Rebound) and production reads none of them. Rebound in particular is the only way to tell 'the interface keeps flapping' from 'the network is fine', and it currently exists only for a test to read.
current_state: bypass.NAT.Stats() is unreachable in production: nothing outside internal/bypass/*_test.go calls it. Verified by grep at the time of writing.

netstack.Stack.Stats() (internal/netstack/netstack.go) folds in natTable's stats but not the bypass NAT's, even though the Stack holds the sink (Config.Bypass). The sink is typed as the netstack.BypassSink interface, which has Send only — so folding it in means either widening that interface or type-asserting for an optional Stats() method. That choice is the task.

Consequence today: the idle sweep of bypass sockets only ever runs on Send (Stats() is the other place it runs from, and nobody calls it), so after traffic stops the sockets persist until Down. Parity with natTable, not a regression — but it is the second reason to wire Stats up.
A neighbour the bypass_tcp_reject pass left: Stats.Rejected now counts bypass-TCP refusals alongside fail-close ones, and nothing in the snapshot distinguishes them.
next_task.goal: Whatever eventually surfaces Stack.Stats (CLI status, metrics) can see bypass socket count, orphaned replies and rebinds. Decide and argue how the sink exposes them: widen netstack.BypassSink, or keep Send-only and type-assert an optional interface.

internal/bypass/bypass.go — Stats() already exists, already sweeps, already documented as unreachable in production (the doc comment says so in as many words; that comment must be corrected by this task, not left behind).

notes.negcheck: runs every guard twice (with/without its policy) via `go test -count=1`; 39 policies as of this pass, ~20-35 min wall clock on this machine — this is expected, not a hang; don't rely on go test's cache. Per-task gate only needs the new policy's own guard under HOP_DISABLE=<name>; the controller runs the full one at the end of the pass.
notes.realtimelint: does not accept ./... as an argument — pass literally `.`
notes.l3_how_to_run: Build once, run under an unprivileged user namespace: `go test -c -o /tmp/l3.test ./internal/l3` then `HOP_L3=1 unshare -Urn /tmp/l3.test` (add `-test.v -test.run '<pattern>'` to scope it). This works without root — unshare -Urn grants CAP_NET_ADMIN inside the fresh netns. Building the test binary once and reusing it across repeated unshare invocations is much faster than `go test` per run when iterating.
